description: Alfr3d greeted the house with "Good morning!" at 10pm. Six different parts of the system each did their own time-of-day math and disagreed, and the voice had no clock at all. They now share one source of truth, built from the household's own wake / sleep / sunrise / sunset routines: it decides when Alfr3d is awake enough to speak, tells the language model what time it actually is (so it won't wish you good morning at night), leads a welcome-home with the right greeting, and lets the small talk wind down in the last stretch before bed. Deployed and verified on the real house system.
The launcher is now "Alfr3d Nexus Launcher" (renamed from "Spatial Launcher" in the in-app About/header copy), tagged v0.1.35.

A pre-submission pass cleared the Play Store technical and policy hygiene: targeting Android 16 (API 36) to meet Google's first-submission requirement, code shrinking and resource minification turned on for release builds and verified on a real device, and a privacy-policy gap closed (an every-15-minute attention-telemetry report to the backend that wasn't disclosed).
Store listing, screenshots, and release notes were rewritten to match everything shipped since the first draft.

Devices window gained the ability to delete a device (tap-to-arm confirm), plus fixes for a chip-row that wrapped instead of scrolling and a connection check that showed a false "connected" state on an http-to-https redirect.
What's left before it goes live is account-holder-only Play Console setup.

milestone: Nexus quick-controls panel for favorite IoT devices
description: Clicking the Nexus Core now opens a top-center panel -- same slide-in language as the existing weather/clock/camera/project-tree side panels -- showing up to 10 favorited smarthome devices as compact toggle/dial tiles, reusing the same device-control endpoint as the Domain page's ControlBlade. A new per-user device_favorites table backs it, capped at 10 devices per user, with an in-panel edit mode to star/unstar. Live-verified end to end in the browser: sign-in gating, star/unstar, tile rendering, and the 10-device cap.

milestone: Full situational-awareness roadmap deployed to production
description: A 12-item situational-awareness roadmap (event log, card feedback, calendar conferencing, a shared context frame, structured cards, per-resident/household anomaly detection, self-hosted routing, plus 3 items investigated and correctly stopped on real evidence -- no ESPHome node, no stable BLE identity, not enough event history yet) shipped to the household's real production box: a real database backup taken first, migrations applied, affected services rebuilt and redeployed, verified live end to end. Also cleared 20+ GB of stale Docker build cache found along the way.

milestone: Learned baselines widened from appliances to residents & the household
description: The one learning mechanism in the system could only ever call an appliance's behavior unusual. It now also learns a household-level "is today unusual" baseline (typical wake/wind-down hours, how many devices are usually online) on top of the new per-resident departure baselines -- same underlying table, same 6-hourly compute job. Real hardware timing was measured on the production box first to make sure the new computation stayed cheap, and it does (about a second added to a job that already ran in well under a minute).

milestone: Leave-by travel guidance rebuilt on self-hosted routing
description: The travel-guidance card removed in August (it needed a paid Google Maps tier that was never configured) is back on different footing: a self-hosted OSRM routing engine plus the public, free Nominatim geocoding API -- no account, no API key, no request leaving the house. Measured directly on the production hardware: a real metro-area map preprocesses in under 2 minutes and serves routes from under 200MB of RAM. Backend live and deployed; the routing engine itself and the launcher's display of the computed leave-by time are still rolling out.
Earliest known concept/build in the Alfr3d lineage.
Early 2014 iteration of the home-automation daemon.
2014 iteration, ordering relative to MK-I/MK-II unconfirmed.
Home-automation daemon running on a Pi (/home/alfr3d/alfr3ddaemon.py), audio handling.
Added Python LIFX integration (pylifx).
Server + mobile companion apps split out: Alfr3dServer, Alfr3d4Android-Original, Alfr3d-MKIII-Android, alfr3d.io.
Separate repo from the 2015 MK-IV Notion page, not yet reconciled with it.
Repo explicitly describes itself as "Successor to Project Alfr3d" -- a rebrand attempt that didn't end up replacing it. Active Feb 2018 to Oct 2020 (239 commits, confirmed via GitHub commit history).

First Kafka message-bus architecture (topics speak/environment/device/user) -- direct architectural precursor to today's Kafka-based backend. Active Sep 2022 through May 2026 (434 commits) -- notably overlapping with the start of the current consolidated rewrite rather than a clean handoff.

milestone: Backend v0.2.0: Auth, secrets, IoT & reliability hardening
description: Full JWT Auth + RBAC shipped and on-device verified across all 5 phases: backend login/refresh/logout, a permission matrix on all 56 write routes, webapp + Nexus Launcher sign-in, and hardening (rate limiting, no username enumeration, self-service/admin password reset).
Every integration credential (Home Assistant, SmartThings, Spotify, ESPHome) is now Fernet-encrypted at rest, with a zero-downtime dual-read fallback for existing plaintext rows.
ESPHome added as a new local-only IoT provider (mDNS discovery, Noise-encrypted API), alongside a device-registry-backed multi-camera streaming model -- tagged v0.2.0 "Multi-Camera Registry".
Household user management landed end to end: self-service profile editing plus a full owner/admin CRUD and password-reset UI for the roster.

Real production fixes along the way: a stalled-ffmpeg self-heal for camera streams, systemd autostart so all 12 containers survive a reboot unattended, and a calendar-sync bug (stray-space name matching, UTC handling).
Consolidated years of prior architectures into today's repo (Littl3-1-Engineering/alfr3d, 534+ commits) -- confirmed to still carry its FSL-1.1-ALv2 LICENSE file.
Two backend services were missed when the secrets-at-rest volume was wired up (found and fixed on the live production box).

First-run onboarding: new installs detect an unclaimed household and walk through claiming a seeded resident or bootstrapping a new owner account, on both the webapp and the Nexus Launcher, instead of a bare login screen.
A durable household event log (previously a 20-item RAM buffer, gone on restart) now backs everything downstream that needs real event history.
A card feedback loop: situational-awareness cards learn when a household ignores them (cooldown + repetition damping), with security-relevant cards exempt from ever being silenced.
A shared per-cycle context frame cut redundant DB reads across the 16+ situational-awareness rules by roughly a third and enabled a new empty-house-but-something's-on check.
Every situational-awareness card gained an additive structured `data` field alongside its display prose, so consumers stop having to regex facts out of it.
Calendar conferencing metadata (real Google Meet/Zoom links) now backs the "call starting soon" card as a confirmed-tier signal, not just a text guess.

Departure-anomaly detection shipped: a resident home well past their typical time with no calendar event explaining it -- the presence-history table this was assumed to need turned out to already exist in the data.

milestone: Nexus Launcher: Pro unlock, theming, rotation lock & write-action sign-in
description: Free spatial launcher with a $5.99 one-time Pro unlock live since v0.1.28, with CI building a debug APK on every push and a signed-release workflow on version tags.
Custom Colors theming: a 5th Pro feature, user-defined accent colors via an in-app HSV picker.
A rotation-lock setting keeps the launcher upright in portrait regardless of device orientation.
Write actions (device control, resident edits, running/editing a routine) now require sign-in, using Keystore-backed credential storage from the Auth + RBAC rollout.

milestone: littl31.com: site launch + copy & scroll-reveal fixes
description: Site live at littl31.com: index.html (pitch), alfr3d.html (product + pricing), lab.html (R&D showcase).
alfr3d.html got real descriptive copy for the Nexus Launcher, Core, Cloud, and Kit cards, plus a fix for a scroll-reveal crash that was silently blocking content sitewide.
Fixed a splash-logo animation crash on the homepage (a stray module-scope reference).

milestone: Pricing strategy: monetization plan → Kit-first → 3 SKUs → CAD-corrected
description: Monetization plan first published: Core free, Nexus Launcher free + $5.99 Pro unlock, Cloud tiers, Kit unscheduled.
Revised to a Kit-first ladder: Kit $399 Founding-100 / $449 steady-state, with a Butler subscription ($9.99/mo) replacing the old Cloud tiers.
Simplified further to exactly 3 paid SKUs by cutting the standalone Relay tier, folding remote access into Butler.
A CAD-verified parts cost check found the Kit underwater on margin at the earlier USD-based estimate -- prompted the hardware pivot above and a revised sales-volume estimate.

Kit hardware base switched from a Raspberry Pi 5 to an N100 mini PC after a cheaper reference build surfaced, dropping parts cost from ~$425 to ~$235 CAD and restoring the margin the Pi 5 + M.2 HAT build had eaten into.
All 3 repos (alfr3d, alfr3d_deck, Littl31) migrated from the personal armageddion account to the Littl3-1-Engineering org.

Build one Kit end-to-end and time assembly before publishing the $399 Founding-100 price. Validates ~$252 landed-cost estimate (Pi 5 8GB, NVMe+HAT, PSU, enclosure, cooling, cabling, packaging, assembly labor, shipping, fees, support/DOA reserve) against a real build, not just parts pricing.

milestone: littl31.com commerce: Stripe Checkout + Founding 100 preorder
description: Top GTM priority: pricing page currently has zero CTA/checkout links on either tier. Add Stripe Checkout for the Kit (Founding 100 preorder with published ship-by date) and Relay/Butler signup + Customer Portal.

alfr3d_deck brought up to alfr3d's baseline: pre-commit-hooks (trailing-whitespace/end-of-file/yaml/large-files) + detect-secrets (fresh baseline, one expected finding -- keystore.properties.sample's changeme placeholders), Dependabot for gradle + github-actions. alfr3d_deck already had CI (build.yml, release.yml) -- ahead of alfr3d there, whose own ci.yml is actually .disabled (a stale claim in this todo corrected). littl31 and Aikido (needs external account signup) still open.

milestone: SmartThings generic IoT control endpoint — fixed, pending live-device verification
description: Fixed 2026-08-24, same day it was found: control_iot_device() (routes/iot.py) now has a source=='smartthings' branch using a new st_utils.translate_generic_control_params() that mirrors the HA translator, mapping ControlBlade's generic command vocabulary to an ST (capability, command, args) triple. sync_st_devices() now also derives device_type via a new st_utils.normalize_st_device_type() from the device's capability list, instead of storing ST's raw deviceTypeName label -- confirmed nothing else in the codebase read that raw label. Both pieces are code-complete and committed; still needs verification against a live SmartThings device, which is the only reason this isn't Shipped yet.
Personality panel currently shows call-count usage only; per-token usage metadata from the LLM client isn't surfaced yet. Minor — a future-enhancement aside, not a scoped plan.
Push notifications to the launcher; depends on Alfr3d Cloud Phase 3 shipping first.
Have the launcher push on-device now-playing (any media session, not just Spotify) to the backend instead of only backend-side polling. Documented as a deferred fast-follow, not yet scoped.
Its own todo/ folder was checked directly and contains only a completed bugfix note (mobile scramble jitter fix); no forward-looking roadmap items exist for the site itself.
Abstract audio-source interface so playback isn't Spotify-only — local library, Tidal, YouTube Music, radio — plus a loose future-ideas list (NLU voice control, Last.fm scrobbling, multi-room sync).
Two more theme options for the existing theme-picker system, on top of the three already shipped (Cyan/Navy, Amber/Charcoal, Light/Teal).

Signing, Gradle Play Publisher, and gated CI already wired up; blocked on manual account-holder steps: Play developer enrollment, Play Console app entry, first manual release upload, sensitive-permission declarations + demo video, hosted privacy policy URL, CI service account for future automated releases.
Attribute calendar/Gmail integrations to individual household members instead of one shared global account. Blocked on Auth + RBAC landing first.
Three parked options beyond the already-shipped HLS pipeline: WebRTC for sub-500ms latency, recorded/archived playback, and computer-vision motion/person detection.
Pre-flashed Raspberry Pi appliance, built to order. Parked until Alfr3d Cloud proves demand. Not yet scheduled.

Remote-access relay (no port forwarding) + push notifications; "thin, dumb-pipe relay" that never sees plaintext data. Now scoped into a phased plan in todo_cloud_relay.md: architecture spike -> subscriber/billing identity + Stripe -> relay/tunnel -> FCM push -> security review. Deliberately a separate identity system from household RBAC auth. Not yet built.

milestone: Personality ticks shouldn't fire on every speak
description: Personality quip "ticks" currently apply to every TTS speak action; should be probabilistic/occasional (random chance, cooldown, or context-based) so it doesn't feel like a bit every time. Newly scoped, not started.

Physical enclosure for the ALFR3D device + peripherals (mic/speaker/camera/sensors), matching the dark tactical/glassmorphic visual identity. Not currently scheduled — blocked on the hardware phase starting and a finalized bill of materials.

milestone: Kit ordering / Cloud signup commerce plan
description: Phased plan to give the Kit and Cloud pricing sections a real path from visitor to paying customer — site currently has zero CTA/checkout links on either tier. Phase A: free waitlist/interest-capture forms. Phase B (gated on Kit waitlist signal): Stripe Checkout for the one-time Kit purchase. Phase C (gated on the Cloud relay being built): Stripe Checkout + Customer Portal + magic-link login alongside the relay's own subscriber identity. Planning only, not started.

milestone: Self-awareness: pronounce own name + don't self-greet
description: Both identity bugs fixed 2026-08-27, not yet on-device verified: normalize_pronunciation() in service_speak regex-substitutes the leetspeak "alfr3d" to "Alfred" right before every TTS call, and update_user_state() in service_user now guards the welcome-greeting flow so the alfr3d system user never announces itself coming online like a household member (its presence-state row still updates normally). A closer look also found the guard is currently dead/defensive code -- no code path in the schema seed or the three runtime user-insert sites ever creates a row with username='alfr3d'.

milestone: CAD BOM correction + revised CAGR/monetization strategy
description: Recommended-tier Kit parts corrected from $191 (a USD-MSRP artifact) to ~$425 CAD verified Canadian pricing -- Founding-100 ($399) now underwater on parts alone before the N100 pivot above. Added a market CAGR range (12-20% working estimate) and a revised pricing/sales plan: budget-tier storage default, Founding-100 reframed as a small hand-assembled batch, Butler subscription as the primary margin engine. Realistic Year 1: 40-100 Kit units; Year 2: 150-400 cumulative.

New situational-awareness card that reads household composition (who's home vs. away, known vs. unknown devices) and surfaces it with urgency-aware styling on the Ambient Brief. Backend check + Deck card both built and unit-tested; not yet verified on-device.

New backend endpoint + routines/now-playing tracking so the launcher can surface a "pick up where you left off" card across surfaces (e.g. resume music paused elsewhere, or a routine edited on the web dashboard). Built and unit-tested; not yet verified on-device.

Learns each device's typical on/off rhythm from history and flags when something is still on well past its usual pattern (e.g. a light on much later than normal). Backend baseline computation + anomaly check built and unit-tested; not yet verified on-device and no real baseline data has accumulated yet.

milestone: Deck: Attention telemetry as a focus signal
description: Launcher reports rolling attention/dwell telemetry to a new backend endpoint, feeding focus and wind-down situational-awareness signals. Built and unit-tested on both sides; not yet verified on-device.

milestone: Explore: Nexus Launcher as a new context source for Alfr3d
description: Explore feeding the launcher's own on-device signals (attention/dwell, foreground app, etc.) back into the backend's situational-awareness engine as a new context source, alongside existing presence/device signals. One candidate signal, BLE presence sensing, was investigated directly and set aside (see "BLE presence sensing -- explored and set aside" above) -- modern phones rotate their Bluetooth address, so nothing personally-carried stayed identifiable in a real scan. The rest of the signal list (WiFi leave/arrive, named context zones, car Bluetooth, etc.) remains unexplored.

milestone: Clean up GitHub CI/CD, security & Aikido CVEs (all repos)
description: CI/CD + security cleanup across all three repos: re-enable alfr3d's disabled ci.yml, finish Aikido signup for littl31, and triage/remediate CVEs Aikido flags once scanning is live across alfr3d, alfr3d_deck, and Littl31. Distinct from Repo tooling standardization (pre-commit/detect-secrets/Dependabot baseline) -- this is the CI pipeline health + vulnerability remediation pass. Not started.

milestone: ESPHome sensors as a situational-awareness signal
description: The ESPHome integration itself has existed since v0.2.0, but nothing in the rule engine reads a sensor yet, and this session's own investigation found zero real ESPHome devices on the household's network to validate against -- picked back up once real hardware exists to test with.

milestone: BLE presence sensing -- explored and set aside
description: The household's hardware can scan for BLE devices just fine, but real scans found no personal device (phone, watch) with a stable enough identity to track -- modern phones deliberately rotate their Bluetooth address. Only fixed smart-home gear (TVs, a smart light) stayed identifiable, which isn't useful as a presence signal. Set aside unless a wearable with a genuinely stable address enters the household.

A planned next step for the household event log -- noticing that one event usually follows another, and gently flagging it when it doesn't -- needs real weeks of history to learn from honestly. The event log itself is brand new, so this is queued rather than built against too little data.
